events.title: A distinct G12D research cluster takes shape
events.summary: Early mechanism studies begin to connect allele-specific signaling with pancreatic cancer models. The cluster is still small, but its vocabulary and experimental systems become more consistent.
events.selectionReason: The fixed dataset crosses the minimum cluster threshold and begins showing repeated entity overlap.

events.title: Structural ideas create a drug-discovery opening
events.summary: Mechanistic work and emerging structural hypotheses start to converge. The replay marks this as an opening rather than proof that the target is druggable.
events.selectionReason: A mechanism node bridges into the first drug-discovery records.

events.title: The field splits into mechanism and intervention tracks
events.summary: One branch continues mapping signaling context while another emphasizes chemical tractability. The two tracks remain linked, but they begin accumulating different methods and publication venues.
events.selectionReason: Graph communities separate while preserving several cross-branch citation links.

events.title: Adaptive signaling complicates the emerging story
events.summary: Combination screens and feedback studies suggest that pathway suppression may trigger compensatory responses. This is displayed as a machine-detected challenge candidate, not a settled contradiction.
events.selectionReason: High debate signals appear in a newly coherent resistance cluster.

events.title: Structure-guided chemistry gains visible momentum
events.summary: Drug-discovery records become denser and more connected to earlier mechanism work. Citation growth accelerates across several related nodes rather than around a single paper.
events.selectionReason: Normalized citation growth and cross-branch connectivity both increase.

events.title: Earlier pathway work returns to the center
events.summary: Older mechanism studies regain attention as combination strategies need explanations for feedback and escape. The replay highlights this as a revival signal based on later connections.
events.selectionReason: Older nodes receive a disproportionate share of links from newer resistance work.

events.title: Clinical translation becomes a separate visible track
events.summary: Early-stage clinical activity appears alongside continuing preclinical optimization. The interface keeps these tracks separate to avoid implying that clinical testing resolves mechanistic uncertainty.
events.selectionReason: Clinical-type records form a persistent branch with target-engagement language.

events.title: Parallel programs accelerate the replay
events.summary: Mechanism, chemistry, and translational branches all add high-impact nodes within a short interval. The result is a field-wide acceleration rather than a single linear breakthrough.
events.selectionReason: Multiple branches show simultaneous growth in node density and normalized impact.

events.title: Combination strategies fan into distinct escape routes
events.summary: Resistance work separates into pathway reactivation, lineage-specific bypass, and immune-context hypotheses. These are exploratory branches and may overlap in real datasets.
events.selectionReason: Resistance nodes form subcommunities with different bridge patterns.

events.title: Dosing and safety constraints reshape expectations
events.summary: Translational records introduce practical constraints that are not visible from potency alone. The replay flags the mismatch between laboratory momentum and clinical feasibility as an interpretive checkpoint.
events.selectionReason: Clinical nodes with constraint language rise while chemistry impact remains high.

events.title: A source update becomes part of the timeline
events.summary: One record carries a structured correction-check marker. In production, this event must come from Crossref or another structured source and must link to that source directly.
events.selectionReason: A structured update status is present in the demo record.

events.title: The field reaches a crowded but unresolved present
events.summary: Multiple clinical programs, biomarker efforts, and resistance hypotheses now coexist. The current view emphasizes open questions rather than declaring a winner or a scientific consensus.
events.selectionReason: All four branches remain active and no single branch dominates every metric.

openQuestions: Which adaptive escape routes are reproducible across models and patient contexts?
How should target engagement, dose intensity, and tolerability be compared across programs?
Which biomarkers separate transient pathway suppression from durable response?
